analysis:
Both units are head-side CHANGELOG.md text (lines 596-1029); only documentation changed, with no executable source, config, or authorization code visible. Nothing in the excerpts changes runtime security behavior.

The prose describes security-relevant behavior this PR may land elsewhere: App Attest dead-key rotation (CHANGELOG.md:611-613), rotation limits and a 6h invalidKey backoff, ready-reply diagnostics outside the signed transcript (616, 620), APNs code-identity retry (614), the macOS 27 durable attestation chain (615), and `darkbloom report` reading credentials under sudo (622). Related threat IDs are TB-002, TB-009, TB-011, T-052..T-058, A-015, A-016, A-017.

The changelog is consistent with the threat model's stated boundary: diagnostics are untrusted and do not grant authorization; rotation never revokes or denies serving; and a rotated key must pass full attestation, receipt, build-qualification and assertion checks (611). Other code files in this PR, if any, must verify these claims. In particular, check the following:
- Rotation admission is serialized with machine merges.
- A new key cannot inherit serving authorization.
- Rotation or enrollment budgets cannot be exhausted by an attacker to strand a provider (T-057).
- Diagnostic fields are bounded and never feed authorization.
- sudo credential reading in `darkbloom report` does not leak tokens into uploaded reports.
- The compatibility claim that the 20-byte CandidateCDHash must match a unique full hash (646) is enforced.

I saw no concrete regression in this documentation-only diff, so no findings are raised. Coverage limit: the underlying code was not supplied.
